 MISSOULA, Mont. — A free holiday concert in partnership with the Missoula Food Bank will bring together local musicians, veterans and community members for an evening of seasonal music and giving.
 It will feature the Missoula Community Concert Band, a group of more than 90 local musicians founded in 1991, and Music Outreach Veterans Engagement Instructional Training, or MOVE-ITT, a new organization led by Richard Little.
 The community band, led by Don Jaramillo, will perform holiday favorites including Leroy Anderson’s “Sleigh Ride,” selections from “Home Alone” and Disney’s “A Christmas Carol,” and a musical narration of “’Twas the Night Before Christmas.”
 MOVE-ITT will perform big band arrangements of “Angels We Have Heard on High,” “White Christmas” and “Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer.” The group draws on the experience of professional musicians from military bands to mentor musicians in preparation, listening and live performance.
 The two groups will close the concert with an audience sing-along.
 Organizers hope the event will become a new Missoula tradition celebrating the holidays through music and community. The concert is free and open to the public. Donations are welcome and will benefit the Missoula Food Bank & Community Center.
 The concert is set for 7 p.m. Saturday, Dec. 5, at ZooTown Church, 3263 Brooks Street.
